summary.tldr: Bill C-61 affirms First Nations jurisdiction over water and wastewater on their lands and sets out standards and principles for safe water services.
what_it_does: Affirms that the inherent right to self-government includes First Nations jurisdiction over water, source water, drinking water, wastewater and related infrastructure on, in and under First Nation lands.
Sets out principles, including substantive equality, to guide clean and safe drinking water and the effective treatment and disposal of wastewater on First Nation lands.
Provides minimum standards for water quality and quantity, and for wastewater effluent.
Provides pathways to help protect source water.
who_it_affects: People living on First Nation lands
summary.background: Bill C-61 was introduced in the House of Commons on 11 December 2023 and was given first reading. It is titled the First Nations Clean Water Act.
